q1_issues.issue: "comparable" is a descriptive (non-classifying) modifier on a plural, which the instruction set distributes over the group's members like a copular predicate; here it is predicated of the group witness itself as (Member $fr comparable).

"the results are high" is a definite plural with a copular predicate, which the instruction set encodes as the group atom PLUS a distributive rule; only (Member sk_result_1 high) is emitted, so a result named later never inherits high.

q2_gaps: generic conditional "P when <clause>": the ConditionalProperty template ("X is P when/at/under/if C") is defined only for an adjective/state or measure/environment condition, and the plain-Implication route says nothing about how a definite-plural copular consequent and its required distribution are encoded inside a rule consequent
notes: The rule is well-formed and fireable - variables bind the maintain event and the flow-rate group, flow_rate is fused as a modifier_noun compound with its rate genus and no exposed noun modifier, Theme is right for "maintained" and (Can $x) for the modal - so the defects are confined to the two plural-distribution omissions.
